text:
It’s the “choice of a lifetime”. The stakes have never been higher. Do you waste 15 minutes of your life reading the second issue of the Reformer, the official monthly newspaper of Reform, every word of which has been written by me, Nigel Farage?
Or do you just throw it straight into the recycling bin?
Make no mistake. If “Backwards with Burnham” gets his way, the EU will insist that every future issue of the Reformer will be written in German. His so-called EU reset “deal” will make every household in the country at least £200,000 worse off each week.
Don’t let the government try to fool you by pointing out that net migration has fallen to its lowest level since 1997. What’s really happening is that foreigners have wised up and are staying away because they don’t want to pay the extortionate amount of money the EU is demanding from the UK. We will only know we have the EU on the run when net immigration is back up over 1 million. Er, hang on …
A UK back in the EU should be unthinkable to every true-born Englishman. So, I’m afraid that rather counts Suella Braverman out. But for the rest of us, the idea of being made to speak French and eat mayonnaise with our chips is an insult to the memory of King George V. A more British king you could not hope to find in a man who was basically German. I didn’t fight in two world wars to take orders from Brussels.
On a side note. Just a month too late, I would like us all to observe a two-minute silence to honour all those Brits who fell in combat. It’s also a time to remind you of my own heroism. On 1 July 1916, I was in command of a regiment on the frontline of the Somme. Shortly before zero hour, I reminded them all of the sacrifices we had to make to save our country. It was just rotten bad luck that as the whistle blew to go over the top, I noticed that one of my shoe laces had become untied. “Dash it, chaps. You go ahead,” I said. And as I bent down, I could feel my back go and I was basically out of combat until 11 November 1918. For my services to the country, I am proud to say I awarded myself the VC and the MC and Bar. Here’s a photo of how I might have looked at the time.
Time now for a change of tone. Enough about me – for the moment. We now move on to our occasional series, Apprentice of the month, in which one of our members recounts their start in life. Today, we hear from Richard “Dicky” Tice, one of our interns at Reform HQ.
“Gosh, yes, it was really exciting. My first day out with all the lads digging trenches on the building site. ‘This is really fun,’ I said to them, as they sat down to drink cups of tea. Or a ‘brew’ as they put it in their charming regional accents. And then, guess what? After three weeks, I must have been doing so well because it turned out that my grandfather ran the company and wanted me to be managing director. So with a bit of hard work, you can get on in life.”
Right, back to me. Here’s a photo of me with the brave women of Piddington. Up until a few months ago, Piddington was a sleepy Oxfordshire village with just 350 inhabitants and a US airbase on its doorstep. The women used to walk around with not a care in the world, mingling with 1,200 airmen, any one of whom could have been a rapist. Now the airbase is being repurposed as a detention centre for migrants from Afghanistan, all of whom could be murderers and rapists, and the village is up in arms. So well done to Piddington for declaring independence from the UK. We look forward to the villagers building their own schools and hospitals.
Here in the Reformer, we – I mean, I – am not afraid to deal with the big issues, including climate change. This is one of the biggest hoaxes being perpetrated on the British people since Brexit. Worse still, it seems that even our fish are being duped. I have personally spoken to several blue-fin tuna and they tell me that they were persuaded to move back to British waters because they were told that the seas around Cornwall had warmed up. But after swimming hundreds of miles north, they found they were still freezing so they jumped into the back of a fishing boat in the hope of getting a hot bath.
Time also for a shout-out to our vetting department. As you know we take vetting very seriously here in Reform. Unlike the Tories who have allowed any number of Cameron cuties – by the way I never said Kemi Badenoch was a Cameron cutie except in this week’s Telegraph – into their party. Brexit, my arse. Excuse my French. The only Brexit betrayer you’ll find in Reform is Robert Jenrick.
That just leaves space for yet another photo of me. This time with my faithful poodle. Dicky likes nothing better than to lie on the floor of my garage while I ignore him. The labrador, of course, sleeps on the bed.

digest_he: העיתונאי ג'ון קרייס מציג טור סאטירי שבו הוא מתייחס למהדורה השנייה של העיתון 'הרפורמר', המנוהל ונכתב על ידי הפוליטיקאי הבריטי נייג'ל פאראג. הטור לועג לטענותיו של פאראג בנוגע להסכמים עתידיים עם האיחוד האירופי, להגירה, ולזיכרונות לכאורה מהיסטוריה צבאית דמיונית. כמו כן, הטקסט מציג בנימה אירונית סיפורים משעשעים לכאורה על פעילים וחברים במפלגה, ומתייחס בסאטיריות לסוגיות כמו משבר האקלים וביקורת פנימית במערכת הפוליטית הבריטית.
